body: **Foco:** Comunicação integrada: Negócios.
**Phrasal verbs:** brush up on.
**Pronúncia:** Organização da informação pela entonação.
**22 palavras novas** (negócios).
**Texto do dia:** editorial / opinião.

blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C1):** eu consigo ler, ouvir, falar e escrever sobre habilidades profissionais a partir de um editorial, usando condicionais e brush up on.

body: Esta aula treina **escrever frases claras e corretas (IELTS Writing, TOEFL Writing)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.title: Editorial: Business English Is a Career Asset
paras: If professionals **had brushed up on** their English earlier, many deals **would have closed** faster. **Unless** companies invest in language training, they **will keep losing** international clients. **Provided that** learners practice regularly, results come quickly.
**Should** leaders doubt the return, **were they to** compare costs with lost contracts, the answer would be obvious.

items.q: Better English would have closed deals faster.
Companies already invest enough in training.

head: Estrutura
Uso
Exemplo
rows: **If they had practiced, deals would have closed.**
**Unless firms invest, they will lose clients.**

blocks.body: Em editoriais, **should / were … to** substituem **if** e soam mais formais.

items.s: If they ___ brushed up on English, deals would have closed. (have, past perfect)
___ companies invest, they will lose clients. (Unless)
___ leaders doubt the return, compare the costs. (Should)
Were they ___ compare costs, the answer would be obvious. (to)

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

body: **Return on investment.** — Retorno sobre o investimento.
**Pay dividends.** — Dar bons resultados.
**Lose ground.** — Perder terreno.
**A competitive edge.** — Vantagem competitiva.
**Speak the same language.** — Falar a mesma língua.
**Get lost in translation.** — Perder-se na tradução.
**Level the playing field.** — Nivelar o jogo.
**Make a case for…** — Defender a ideia de…
**Unless we invest in training, it will happen again.** — A menos que invistamos em treinamento, vai acontecer de novo.
**Should leaders doubt the return, compare the lost contracts.** — Se os líderes duvidarem do retorno, comparem com os contratos perdidos.
**Were they to do that, the answer would be obvious.** — Se fizessem isso, a resposta seria óbvia.

forms: I / you / we / they invest in

Significado
Exemplo
rows: I need to brush up on my English. — Preciso reciclar meu inglês.

blocks.title: Editorial desk
lines: If staff had brushed up on English, we would have won that deal.
Se a equipe tivesse revisado o inglês, teríamos ganhado aquele negócio.
Unless we invest in training, it will happen again.
A menos que invistamos em treinamento, vai acontecer de novo.
Should leaders doubt the return, compare the lost contracts.
Se os líderes duvidarem do retorno, comparem com os contratos perdidos.

Se fizessem isso, a resposta seria óbvia.

blocks.title: Pronúncia: Organização da informação pela entonação

items.label: Organização da informação pela entonação
items.note: A entonação organiza o discurso: queda = informação completa; subida = há mais por vir; a informação nova recebe o foco (nuclear stress).

prompts.model: If we had prepared, we would have won.
Should you need help, call me.
Were we to fail, we would adapt.

blocks.task: Write a 90-word editorial paragraph recommending language training, with two conditional structures.
blocks.model: If professionals had brushed up on their English earlier, many deals would have closed faster. Unless companies invest in language training, they will keep losing international clients. Provided that learners practice regularly, results come quickly. Should leaders doubt the return, they need only compare the cost of training with the cost of lost contracts.

items.why: **return on investment** = retorno sobre o investimento.

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
